title: Brown marmorated stink bug on fruits

Header: Brown marmorated stink bug on fruits
Halyomorpha halys brown marmorated stink bug, BMSB, 臭板子臭大姐臭娘娘 in Chinese

Prevention: Sometimes leave litter removal is recommended, but it has little effect as most bugs overwinter on trunks and walls and not in debris.
Bag close-to- ripening peaches, apricots or apples with bags (such as
Ltd., or others) in sunny period between 9:00 to 11:00am or 2:00 to 6:00pm to protect against piercings.
Monitoring: Stink bugs attack many fruits, but most seriously apricot, cherries, and peaches.
Survey 10-20 fruit trees per hectare every 2 nd week.
Search for young branches, leaves and buds that are wilting.
Therefore, search on wilted parts for 1 to 1.5 cm long, ½ to 1 cm wide, oval, flattened bugs (v-shaped back) in various shades of brown on top and undersides, with grey, black markings.
August search for egg masses underside leaves.
If 4 to 6 egg masses found per tree, consider action 2 weeks later.

Use sex pheromone traps (shun - 12-16 carbon diene - 1 – alcohol 顺- 12 - 碳二 烯-1- 丙醇; 1 trap per ha, 2/3rd tree height) to lure adult bugs, if 20 to 40 bugs are trapped per week prior fruit ripening, you may consider action
Bugs pierce and suck on fruits, which causes uneven hard scab wounds on fruit surface.
If seen, action is too late this season.
If 5 to 8 fruits per 100 fruits were damaged consider biological action for the following season.
Direct Control: Trap bugs in their overwintering sites.
Fold cardboard-carton and fix them onto sun- exposed walls near the orchard (around mid to late
September) wherein bugs will hide in winter.

Spray azadirachtin- products before high incidence of adult bugs over leaves during sunny wheather (usually 0.3% products at a dose of 9.0-10.8g per ha)
Restrictions: Because the bugs pierce fruits and then feed, only contact insecticides that reach the body of the insect may have some effects.
Systemic pesticides are not an option at fruiting stage because of residues inside fruits.
In general, insecticides are rarely used against stink bugs.
When using a chemical or botanical pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
